Course: 2026/2027

What does it all mean? An introduction to philosophy
(11692)
Dual Bachelor Data Science and Engineering - Telecommunication Technologies Engineering (Study Plan 2020) (Plan: 456 - Estudio: 371)


Coordinating teacher: LABANDEIRA MORAN, SIBLEY ANNE

Department assigned to the subject: Humanities: Philosophy, Language, Literature Theory Department

Type: Courses of humanities
ECTS Credits: 3.0 ECTS

Course: 1º
Semester:



Requirements (Subjects that are assumed to be known)
This is an introductory course, so previous specific knowledge is not required.
Objectives
Competence and skills that will be acquired: - Familiarity with philosophical problems, as well as the cultural and scientific contexts in which they arise -Familiarity with basic philosophical terminology ¿ - Skills for philosophical argumentation and conceptual reasoning to address these problems ¿ - Reading comprehension of simple classical philosophical texts
Description of contents: programme
I. Introduction 1. Basic information on the course 2. What is Philosophy? II. Knowing 1. Truth and error. How can we know what is real? 2. Reality, language and concepts. II. Knowing yourself. 1. Who am I? About oneself. 2. Freedom, mind and body. III. Ethics and the Good Life 1. Good and evil. 2. Living together. 3. Where do emotions fit in?
Learning activities and methodology
Learning activities: -THEORETICAL CLASSES - 1.5 ECT (100% assistance) -EXAM - 1.5 ECT (100% assistance) Students have the option to request tutorial sessions, within the office hours specified in Aula Global. The methodology will include: THEORETICAL CLASSES. Lectures by the teacher with the support of audiovisual and digital media, to develop the key contents of the course. Bibliography and other learning materials will be provided either in class or via Aula Global. PRACTICAL EXERCISES. There will be debates and guided activities about authors, theories, philosophical problems, etc. for students to develop individually and in groups.
Assessment System
  • % end-of-term-examination/test 60
  • % of continuous assessment (assigments, laboratory, practicals...) 40
